The only values ever placed in `outcomes` are the three grade literals, and their lexicographic order ("unverifiable" < "verifiable" < "verified") coincides element for element with the _RANK order (0 < 1 < 2), so natural-order min selects the same worst grade for every possible combination. Should a grade ever be renamed out of that coincidence the mutant becomes killable and this entry fails as stale, which is the intended alarm.

_build_memory_content discards its cwd parameter on its first line (`_ = cwd`) and never reads it again, so the memory body is identical whatever cwd value it receives.
_should_capture decides from tool_name and len(output) only; its tool_input parameter is never read in its body, so passing None returns the same (should, reason) pair for every event.

The default only applies to an event with no tool_response. A 4-character output is below the 50-character floor for every tool whose memory includes output (high-value and network tools are skipped), light-value tools never put output in the body, and 'xxxx' contains none of the words _build_tags looks for, so the stored memory is identical.

ElementTree names a qualified tag `{uri}local` and an unqualified one without braces; a local name (an XML NCName) cannot contain `}`, and ElementTree's expat parser, which uses `}` as its namespace separator, rejects a namespace URI containing `}` (measured 2026-11-06, CPython 3.11 xml.etree: xmlns:a="urn:p}q" raises ParseError, "urn:pq" parses). A parsed tag therefore holds at most one `}`, so splitting from the left or the right, with or without maxsplit=1, yields the same last field. No parsed input distinguishes the variants.

`handler` replaces any `period` outside ("day", "week", "month", "all") with "week" on the next statement.
